author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Sanjay Sah was released from a Kathmandu hospital Friday after surviving nine days trapped inside a tunnel at Nepal’s Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower station. Floods and mudslides struck the Bhotekoshi River area and tore through the facility, leaving the 30-year-old mechanical foreman isolated deep inside the mountainside powerhouse.

Sah told Reuters that he had no food and survived by drinking floodwater and water seeping from the mountain rock. He spent long periods with his eyes closed because darkness and debris made movement hazardous. From an opening on the fifth floor of the six-story structure, he shouted in hopes of finding other survivors but heard no response.

Rescuers reached Sah on the 10th day after the disaster. He said thoughts of his wife, young daughter and wider family helped him maintain hope. The rescue provided a rare positive outcome after the late-August collapse of a Himalayan glacier caused widespread destruction across Nepal and China’s Tibet region, where authorities have reported heavy loss of life and thousands missing.
dek: Sanjay Sah said he survived without food by drinking floodwater and seepage before rescuers reached the mountain hydropower station.
headline: Nepal tunnel survivor leaves hospital after nine-day ordeal
